description: Wire the i18n layer from FEAT-001 into the whole frontend UI: mount I18nProvider, add a JA / EN language toggle in the header, and replace every hard-coded Japanese UI string in App.tsx and all components with t()/lang-aware helper calls so the entire visible UI (buttons, labels, status, evolution conditions, battle results/log, chat, speech bubble, evolution banner, aria-labels) renders in the selected language and switches synchronously. Persistence and default come from FEAT-001 (localStorage 'ddm.lang', default 'ja'). This feature does NOT touch chat-AI language (FEAT-003). JA output must remain byte-identical to today so the existing demo is unchanged when lang='ja'. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: In packages/frontend/src/main.tsx: wrap <App /> with <I18nProvider> from ./i18n.ts so the whole tree can call useI18n().

In packages/frontend/src/App.tsx: call useI18n(). Replace the header h1 text 'デジタルモンスター育成' with t('app.title'). Add a language toggle control in <header className="app-header"> next to/below the title: two buttons (or a segmented control) labeled 'JA' and 'EN' that call setLang('ja')/setLang('en'); mark the active one (e.g. aria-pressed and an 'active' class). Replace loading text '読み込み中…', the null-monster text 'モンスターを準備できませんでした。', and the footer '進化条件: トレーニング回数 ＋ 経過時間 ／ セーブは自動です' with t() lookups. For the SpeechBubble baby text, replace BABY_SPEECH_TEXT with babySpeechText(lang) so the baby bubble is localized. Keep the care-fx logic unchanged.

In packages/frontend/src/components/CarePanel.tsx: accept the current lang (via useI18n() inside the component, or as a prop from App) and replace 'お世話' (also the aria-label), '餌やり', 'トレーニング', '睡眠'/'起こす' toggle labels, '清掃', and the care-hint paragraph with t() lookups. Keep emojis and button class names unchanged.

In packages/frontend/src/components/StatsPanel.tsx: localize 'きぶん: ' prefix (use moodLabel(monster, lang) for the value), the aria-label 'ステータス', the stat labels '攻撃'/'防御' (HP stays 'HP'), 'トレーニング回数: ', the evolution block title '進化条件', the final-stage line '最終段階（{stageLabel(stage, lang)}）', '次の段階: {nextLabel for lang}', the 'トレーニング {cur}/{req}' line label, and the '経過 {formatMinutes(elapsed, lang)}/{formatMinutes(required, lang)}' line label. Use evolutionProgress's nextLabelJa/nextLabelEn (or stageLabel) per lang. Numbers/stat values stay as-is.

In packages/frontend/src/components/BattlePanel.tsx: localize 'バトル' (heading + aria-label), the button '⚔️ 野生のモンスターと戦う', and switch the enemy name and log/winner rendering to lang-aware helpers: enemyName uses stageLabel(stage, lang) with a localized 'wild {label} monster' template (JA stays '野生の{label}モンスター'), log lines use battleLogLine(..., lang) and the winner headline uses winnerLabel(winner, lang). Keep the structured-English intermediate string the component builds for battleLogLine (it already round-trips through the parser), but ensure the player/enemy names injected are the localized display names so lines read naturally.

In packages/frontend/src/components/ChatPanel.tsx: localize '会話' (heading + aria-label), the disabled hint, the empty-log prompt '話しかけてみよう！', the input placeholder 'メッセージを入力', the input aria-label 'メッセージ', and the '送信' button. Keep the modelId display as-is.

In packages/frontend/src/components/EvolutionBanner.tsx: localize '進化した！ {stage} になった！' (use stageLabel(stageId, lang)) and the close-button aria-label '閉じる'. Compose the EN sentence naturally (e.g. 'Evolved! Became {Stage}!').

In packages/frontend/src/components/SpeechBubble.tsx: it is presentational and receives text from App; no string changes needed beyond confirming App now passes babySpeechText(lang). Leave as-is if no literals exist.

Add minimal CSS in packages/frontend/src/styles.css for the header language toggle (e.g. a .lang-toggle container and active-state styling) consistent with the existing dark theme; do not restructure existing rules.

Manually sanity check by building the frontend (`npm run build -w @ddm/frontend`) and, if practical, running the existing e2e/serve helper under .agents/tasks/task-digital-monster/ is NOT required; rely on the build + the FEAT-001 unit tests. Ensure no remaining hard-coded Japanese user-facing literal exists in App.tsx or components (search for Japanese characters in those files and confirm each remaining one is a dictionary value, a code comment, or a non-UI string).
acceptance_criteria: main.tsx wraps App in I18nProvider; App renders a JA/EN toggle in the header that calls setLang and visibly marks the active language.

Switching the toggle to EN re-renders the ENTIRE visible UI in English (header, loading/error, care buttons+hint, stats labels+mood, evolution-condition block, battle heading/button/enemy name/log/winner, chat heading/hint/placeholder/empty-prompt/send, speech bubble baby text, evolution banner) and switching back to JA restores the exact original Japanese.
The selected language persists across reloads via localStorage key 'ddm.lang' and defaults to 'ja' on first load.
No user-facing hard-coded Japanese string literal remains in App.tsx or any component in packages/frontend/src/components (verified by inspection); aria-labels are also localized.
`npm run build` from repo root exits 0 and all FEAT-001 tests still pass (JA output unchanged).
verification: From repo root: `npm run build` exits 0 (frontend tsc + vite build included).
From repo root: `npm test` (shared) and `cd packages/frontend && env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --experimental-strip-types --test src/game-ui.test.ts` both pass with 0 failures.

grep for CJK characters in packages/frontend/src/App.tsx and packages/frontend/src/components/*.tsx and confirm every match is inside i18n.ts dictionary usage, a comment, or a non-UI identifier (no stray UI literal).
